documents.title: AI at Smith: Students
documents.stance_why: The page says 'Policies vary by course and professor' and tells students to 'know your course policy' and ask when in doubt, so the college sets no AI rule itself and hands the decision to professors, which is delegates.
documents.summary: Student-facing page of five expectations for generative AI at Smith: know the course policy, disclose and cite, verify, guard data, and embrace difficulty, plus support resources. It sets no college-wide ban or permission and defers to each course.

units.why: The heading 'Know your course policy' tells students it is their job to find out the rules for each course, which is P78; P10 (ask when unsure) is a separate bullet.
units.anchor: Know your course policy
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on every code. They differed only in wording: coder A kept the anchor with its list number and no policy; coder B added a normalized policy. The heading 'Know your course policy' already states the rule, so the policy is null and the anchor drops the numeral.

units.why: "Policies vary by course and professor" states that the rule is set per course and instructor and the page sets none itself, so P04, informs.
units.anchor: Policies vary by course and professor
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded actor all, phase general; coder B coded student, course-start. The sentence 'Policies vary by course and professor' is a fact about where AI rules are set, true for everyone and stated as a principle, not an instruction to students (the instruction is the separate 'Know your course policy' unit), so all/general/informs.

units.why: 'When in doubt, ask your professor before using AI for a class project' is the ask-first rule in P10, addressed to students and tied to doing coursework.
units.anchor: When in doubt, ask your professor before using AI for a class project
units.frag_end: using AI for a class project

units.why: "Ask proactively to discuss course expectations and whether AI tools should be part of that process" asks students to start the conversation even without doubt; nearest type is P10 but it is broader than "when unsure".
units.anchor: Ask proactively to discuss course expectations and whether AI tools should be part of that
units.fit_note: Asks students to raise AI expectations proactively with the instructor, not only when unsure. / Students are told to proactively open a discussion about expectations and whether AI should be part of the course process, not only to ask when unsure.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded unit_stance neutral, coder B encourage. The line asks students to raise AI expectations with the professor; it takes no position on whether AI is used ('whether AI tools should be part of that process'), so neutral. Both coders agreed on actor, phase, modality (should) and type P10, with the same fit note.

units.why: "Cite and disclose AI use like other outside sources" requires acknowledgment of AI use, so P24 (disclose with each submission); the "like other outside sources" analogy is secondary.
units.anchor: Cite and disclose AI use like other outside sources
units.fit_note: Frames AI like any other outside source (P45 analogy).

units.why: 'Document prompts and tool contributions' asks students to record the prompts and what the tool contributed, which is the prompt/tool detail of P25 rather than full transcripts (P26).
units.anchor: Document prompts and tool contributions
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded unit_stance neutral, coder B permit. 'Document prompts and tool contributions' is a condition attached to using AI, like the sibling cite-and-disclose unit that both coders coded permit, so permit for consistency.

units.why: 'Demonstrate your own thinking so your professors can respond to you and help you learn' keeps the student as the visible thinker, which is P32; the purpose is so professors can respond.
units.anchor: Demonstrate your own thinking so your professors can respond to you

units.why: 'Keep a human in the loop and check AI-generated information before sharing' tells students to verify AI output, so P31.
units.anchor: Keep a human in the loop and check AI-generated information before sharing
units.fit_note: Also asks that a human stay in the loop.

units.why: 'Verify claims and check sources' with the reason 'AI tools predict language patterns, not facts' is a verify-output rule with a stated reason, P31.
units.anchor: Verify claims and check sources
units.policy: Students verify claims and check sources because AI tools predict language patterns, not facts.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on every code. They differed only in the normalized policy wording; the final policy keeps the stated reason ('AI tools predict language patterns, not facts') and adds nothing.

units.why: 'Misinformation is always possible—treat responses as a starting point' warns that AI output can be wrong and should not be accepted as final, P31 (sibling bullet to the verify rule, a different point: treat output as a draft).
units.anchor: Misinformation is always possible—treat responses as a starting point

units.why: "Protect personal information and sensitive research data" is a data-protection duty, P50.
units.anchor: Protect personal information and sensitive research data
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded should/neutral, coder B must/restrict. The line sits among 'Five things for students to remember', an advisory list; the hard prohibition is the separate 'Never enter private data' line, which both coded must-not. 'Protect personal information' is therefore should, with neutral unit_stance because it takes no position on AI use itself.

units.why: 'Never enter private data in public unsupported AI platforms' is a flat prohibition on private data in unsupported tools, P50 (data protection and tool vetting).
units.anchor: Never enter private data in public unsupported AI platforms

units.why: 'Google Workspace is college approved—use Google Gemini and Notebook with your Smith ID' points students to the college-approved tools, which is P92 (institution-wide tools, not a single course).
units.anchor: Google Workspace is college approved—use Google Gemini and Notebook with your Smith ID
units.frag_end: with your Smith ID to protect your data
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on every code. Coder A anchored only the instruction; coder B anchored the full sentence and wrote a normalized policy. The anchor 'Google Workspace is college approved--use Google Gemini and Notebook with your Smith ID' states the rule on its own, so the policy is null.

units.why: 'Seek out friction in the learning process—wrestling with ideas supports real cognitive growth' gives desirable difficulty as a reason to do the thinking yourself, P41.
units.anchor: Seek out friction in the learning process

units.why: 'Cultivate your own unique voice to say the things that only you can say' asks students to develop their own voice; no type covers voice or perspective as a goal (P32 is about being the problem-solver), so UNCOVERED.

units.uncovered_note: Students should develop and keep their own unique voice, framed as a value rather than a skill or integrity rule. / Students are urged to cultivate their own unique voice and perspective rather than outsourcing it to AI.

units.anchor: Interns will provide AI training to students
units.frag_end: conversations around AI and higher education.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded phase general, coder B over-time, and only B wrote a policy. The sentence announces an institutional training offer, not a review or revision, so general. The anchor 'Interns will provide AI training to students' states it, so the policy is null.

units.why: The Jacobson Center is listed for 'writing guidance, brainstorming, planning, and support for revising your writing', directing students to human writing support, P72.
units.anchor: For writing guidance, brainstorming, planning, and support for revising your writing.

units.why: Libraries: "Work with Subject Librarians to find authoritative and reliable sources" directs students to human help, P72.
units.anchor: Work with Subject Librarians to find authoritative and reliable sources.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded modality should, coder B informs. 'Work with Subject Librarians to find authoritative and reliable sources' is phrased as an imperative to students, unlike the descriptive Jacobson Center line next to it, so should.

units.why: 'Reach out to your professors or class dean when feeling uncertain about policies or overwhelmed by coursework' directs students to human help; P72 fits, although the 'overwhelmed' part also touches P99.

units.fit_note: Also names being overwhelmed by coursework as a reason to seek help, which touches reducing pressure that leads to misuse (P99).

documents.title: AI at Smith: Faculty and Staff

units.resolution_why: Coder A coded all/general, coder B admin/before-course. The committee and working groups are named as the college bodies doing set-up work on guidance, so admin and before-course. The anchor states the fact on its own, so the policy is null.

units.why: The sentence sets the scope of the guidance, 'responsibly at Smith, whether that's in teaching, research, administration, or operations', a framework statement P56; the committee in the same sentence is coded separately as P80.
units.anchor: guidance on using AI responsibly at Smith, whether that’s in teaching, research, administration, or operations

The source says the committee leads efforts 'to provide clear, thoughtful guidance on using AI responsibly at Smith, whether that's in teaching, research, administration, or operations'. notes: Reconciled from coder A (66 units) and coder B (63 units); 60 matched, 6 only-A and 3 only-B units, all kept after checking the source text. The three pages are Smith's AI at Smith student and faculty/staff pages and the Academic Integrity Board faculty page. The AIB reporting and sanction passages are generic integrity procedure on a page that handles generative AI cases, so they were coded. The students page does not itself say AI is assumed not allowed, so no default-prohibit unit was coded. No school, computing or course documents were found (course layer deferred). Neither coder proposed new types. Recurring UNCOVERED candidates for later review: a student's own voice as a value (students page, AIB page) and the Board keeping records of cases / recognizing AI papers by lack of voice. Fit notes from both coders were kept.
